title: Exit Reason and the Posted Final Cycle in C&I Exit Damages
content:
For Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, the exit damages rate is scaled by the exit reason once the cycle that ends on the close date has been posted: a final bill (close reason final billed) with that cycle posted scales it by 0.85, another supplier's enrollment (close reason switched to other supplier) with that cycle posted scales it by 1.05, and any other case leaves it unscaled. Scaling multiplies the exit damages rate per kWh by the figure shown.

The cycle that ends on the close date has been posted when the contract carries a supply line whose billing period end is the close date.

| Close reason | Supply line with a billing period end on the close date | Exit damages rate multiplied by |
|---|---|---|
| final billed | posted | 0.85 |
| final billed | not posted | 1, unscaled |
| switched to other supplier | posted | 1.05 |
| switched to other supplier | not posted | 1, unscaled |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A switch-away closed on 17 March 2026 whose cycle 16 February to 17 March 2026 is on the bill: a rate of $0.0060 per kWh becomes 0.0060 multiplied by 1.05, that is $0.0063 per kWh.
